Method of Attack: Remote Access Trojan (RAT) installation to gain remote access, steal sensitive information, conduct network reconnaissance, disable security software, and prepare for more potent payloads
Impacted Systems: Systems vulnerable to Microsoft Office Equation Editor CVE-2017-11882 exploit
Attack Vector: Phishing emails with malicious attachments (ZIP archive, macro-laced Excel file)
Exploitation of Microsoft Office Equation Editor vulnerability CVE-2017-11882
Indicators of Compromise: ZIP attachment containing Agent Tesla RAT
Phishing emails originating from Netherlands (83%) targeting Czech Republic, South Korea, Germany, UK, US
Phishing emails originating from German IPs (89%) targeting Ireland, India, US
